feature: Marketing Free Scan scoped Prospect account (/scan/account + the acctScreen block on /scan/remediate) — Git #4329, Feature #1352. A paid Free Scan Prospect creates a SCOPED login (emailed code -> password -> authenticator app or SMS) that opens only their own engagement: scan results, signed SOW and the Remediate step behind it. It is not a Portal login: the credential lives in free_scan_accounts (never users.password_hash / mfa_enrollments / client_services, so hasRealEntitlement() #656 stays closed) and the session is an httpOnly cookie scoped to /api/public/free-scan, signed with a derived key requireAuth cannot verify. Served by routes/public-free-scan-account.ts -> lib/free-scan-account.ts, plus the `accountSession` door on resolveActor (routes/public-free-scan-sow.ts).
notes: SCOPE OF THIS MANIFEST — what a browser and an HTTP client can assert with no seeded data:
1. The refusal contract of every /api/public/free-scan/account/* route and of the new
`accountSession` door on the existing Remediate and SOW reads (apiTests): no credential is
still 400 credential_required, a malformed sessionId is 400 session_invalid, and asking for the
account door with no session cookie is 401 account_signin_required. Sign-in with an unknown
address is 401 invalid_credentials (the same answer a wrong password gets), and a forged or
garbage login challenge is 401 challenge_invalid.
2. /scan/account renders the sign-in screen for a visitor with no session, and never the
engagement page (uiSteps).
3. /scan/remediate for a visitor with nothing still shows 'We lost track of your scan', now with
a 'Sign in to your engagement' link to /scan/account (uiSteps).
WHAT IS NOT ASSERTED HERE, and why:
The account flow itself needs a signed, PAID engagement (Stripe), a real mailbox for the emailed
code and an authenticator for the TOTP code. Faking those from a manifest would be coverage of a
fixture. They are covered instead by:
artifacts/api-server/src/routes/public-free-scan-account.live-db.test.ts — against live Postgres:
unpaid refusal, code -> password -> TOTP enrollment -> session cookie, the SCOPE assertions (no
users.password_hash, no client_services row, no mfa_enrollments row, requireAuth's JWT_SECRET
cannot verify the session), the account door opening Remediate, no re-creation of a completed
account, sign-out revoking server-side, password + TOTP sign-in, and the lockout.
A recorded headless-Edge run (build #4329, 2026-09-16) of the real pages against an isolated
api host + the marketing Vite: acctScreen code/password/MFA screens -> write-consent stage with
the decline copy pointing at the engagement page -> guide with 'Open your engagement' ->
/scan/account engagement page -> /scan/review and /scan/results through the account session ->
sign out -> sign in with password + authenticator code; /api/portal/pillars stayed 401 from the
signed-in tab.
The login route writes a free_scan_account_sign_in_failed audit row per run of step 6; that is the
real behaviour being asserted, not a side effect to suppress.

RECOVERY (Git #4483, sessionTag 4483-recovery) — asserted here: send-code answers 202 for an address with no account (no oracle) and 400 for a malformed one; verify-code refuses an unknown address with the same 400 code_invalid a wrong code gets; every token-bearing step refuses a garbage recovery token 401 recovery_expired; the AdminV2 queue refuses an anonymous caller 401; and /scan/account opens both recovery paths from the sign-in card.

NOT asserted here, and why: the recovery flow itself needs a complete engagement account, a real mailbox for the emailed code, an authenticator and a platform-admin approval. It is covered against live Postgres by artifacts/api-server/src/routes/public-free-scan-account-recovery.live-db.test.ts — no-oracle send/verify, resend gap and daily cap, attempt budget, emailed code alone cannot re-enrol, password reset revokes sessions without signing in, factor-reset request needs the password and consumes the token, a password reset cancels an approved factor reset, an expired approval re-enrols nothing, and the approved replacement swaps the factor, revokes sessions and signs in.
